title.narrative: Enhancing legitimate stability and human security in Africa: continental,regional and national approaches

description.narrative:
Outcome 1: Enhanced decision-making knowledge and capacity at the continental (AU), regional (RECs) and national (Ethiopia) levels.
Outocme 2: Informed political and thematic dialogue on African peace, security and governance issues.
Outcome 3: Inclusive, transparent and effective governance at the continental, regional and national levels.
The project aims at supporting continental, regional and national efforts to promote peace, stability and good governance in Africa.

comment.narrative: At least one retreat held for the AU member states Technical Experts

The ISS organized a retreat for the AU member states Technical Experts on the theme " Peace support operations in Africa - Where are we and what is next" . The objective was to provide an opportunity to assess the state of peace support operations in Africa from the perspective of examining achievements, challenges, and future projections and to deepen the understanding of Technical Experts on the concepts and experiences surrounding peacekeeping and peace enforcement in Africa and help them deduce lessons that can inform the review of APSA and the ensuing debate on the future of UN peace operations, with the objective of shaping continental policy around the use of PSOs in the search for peace.

title.narrative: Public seminars organized for key stakeholders and policy makers

description.narrative: Number of seminars held

comment.narrative: At least one seminar held on summit of the Future

The ISS organized two Seminars on the Summit of the Future; 1. In collaboration with UN-OAU on the theme " Amplifying Africa’s Peace and Security Priorities in the Pact for the Future". The objective was to contribute to preparations for the inter-governmental negotiations in the lead-up to the Summit for Future which was to be held in New York on the margins of the General Assembly 2. In collaboration with UN-OSAA on the theme " Unpacking the Pact for the Future and its Implications for Africa. The objective was to delve into the critical outcomes of the Pact, exploring their implications for the continent's peace and security, governance, and socio-economic development, as well as its standing in the global arena. 3. In collaboration with UN-OSAA - Closed seminar on the theme "Building and Promoting African Consenus for the Summit of the Future' The objective was to facilitate open exchanges among members of Africa’s diplomatic community in Addis Ababa, New York, and Brussels on how the continent can refine its priorities and position itself in making strategic input into the ongoing process.

The ISS organized two open seminars: 1. On the theme : "Can the Ukraine Conflict build bridges between Africa and Europe" The objectiv was to take stock of the evolution and current dynamics of the Africa-EU partnerships as well as build bridges of understanding between Africa and Europe in the context of the ongoing Russia-Ukraine conflict. 2. On the theme: "Over coming electoral Challenges in Africa". The objective was to interrogate electoral processes and elections in Africa, evaluate the policies and strategies available at the continental and regional levels and provide targeted recommendations as to how best the AU and RECs can support countries to address electoral challenges in the short, medium and long term
